nodes.name: Theorem 3.1
Corollary 3.10
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma_{0}\in\mathbb{Z}[i]$ with $\gamma_{0}\neq 0$ and let $(\gamma_{1},\gamma_{2},\gamma_{3},\gamma_{4})\in\mathbb{Z}[i]^{4}$ be an admissible 4-tuple. Then for any partition of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ into finitely many cells, there exist $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{Z}[i]$ such that $\gamma\gamma_{0}(\alpha+\gamma_{1}\beta)(\alpha+\gamma_{2}\beta)$ and $\gamma\gamma_{0}(\alpha+\gamma_{3}\beta)(\alpha+\gamma_{4}\beta)$ are distinct and nonzero, and they belong to the same cell.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.11
nodes.statement:
(The general solution for a special class of equations).
  If $p$ is a quadratic equation satisfying the condition in Theorem 3.1, then there exists an admissible 4-tuple $(\gamma_{1},\gamma_{2},\gamma_{3},\gamma_{4})\in\mathbb{Z}[i]^{4}$ such that for all $\gamma',\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{Z}[i]$, the elements $x=\gamma'\gamma_{0}(\alpha+\gamma_{1}\beta)(\alpha+\gamma_{2}\beta)$ and $y=\gamma'\gamma_{0}(\alpha+\gamma_{3}\beta)(\alpha+\gamma_{4}\beta)$
  satisfy $p(x,y,n)=0$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}[i]$, where $\gamma_{0}\in\mathbb{Z}[i],\gamma_{0}\neq 0$.

Theorem 5.1
nodes.statement:
($U^{2}$ decomposition theorem).
  For every $\epsilon>0$, there exist positive integers $Q=Q(\epsilon),R=R(\epsilon),N_{0}=N_{0}(\epsilon)$ such that for $N\geq N_{0}$, there exists a kernel $\phi_{N,\epsilon}$ on $R_{\tilde{N}}$ with the following property:
  For every $\chi\in\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{Z}[i]}$, writing $\chi_{N,s}=\chi_{N}*\phi_{N,\epsilon}$ and $\chi_{N,u}=\chi_{N}-\chi_{N,s}$, we have

  (i)$\vert\chi_{N,s}(\alpha+Q)-\chi_{N,s}(\alpha)\vert, \vert\chi_{N,s}(\alpha+Qi)-\chi_{N,s}(\alpha)\vert\leq\frac{R}{N}$ for every $\alpha\in R_{\tilde{N}}$;

  (ii)$\Vert\chi_{N,u}\Vert_{U^{2}(R_{\tilde{N}})}\leq\epsilon$.

  Moreover, for every $N\in\mathbb{N}, \bold{\xi}\in R_{\tilde{N}}$ and $0<\epsilon'\leq\epsilon$, we have $\widehat{\phi_{N,\epsilon'}}(\bold{\xi})\geq\widehat{\phi_{N,\epsilon}}(\bold{\xi})\geq 0$.

nodes.name: Corollary 6.9
nodes.statement:
(Modified $U^{3}$-inverse theorem).
  For every $\epsilon>0$, there exist $\delta=\delta(\epsilon)>0, M=M(\epsilon),N_{0}=N_{0}(\epsilon)\in\mathbb{N}$ and a finite family $\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}(\epsilon)$ of nilmanifolds of order 2, of dimension at most $M$ and having a vertical torus of dimension 1, such that: for every $N\geq N_{0}$, if $f\colon R_{\tilde{N}}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ is a function with $\vert f\vert\leq 1$ and $\Vert f\Vert_{U^{3}(R_{\tilde{N}})}\geq\epsilon$, then either

  (i) $\Vert f\Vert_{U^{2}(R_{\tilde{N}})}\geq\delta$; or

  (ii) there exists a nilmanifold $X$ belonging to the family $\mathcal{H}$, a polynomial map $g\colon\mathbb{Z}^{2}\rightarrow G$ of degree 2 with respect to the filtration $G_{\bullet}$, and a nilcharacter $\bold{\psi}$ of $X$ with frequency 1, such that $\Vert\bold{\psi}\Vert_{\mathcal{C}^{2m}(X)}\leq 1$ and $\Bigl\vert\mathbb{E}_{m+ni\in R_{\tilde{N}}}f(m+ni)\bold{\psi}(g(m,n)\cdot e_{X})\Bigr\vert\geq\delta$.

Theorem 6.8
nodes.statement:
(The inverse theorem for $\mathbb{Z}^{2}$ actions). For every $\epsilon>0$, there exists $\delta=\delta(\epsilon)>0, N_{0}=N_{0}(\epsilon)\in\mathbb{N}$ and a nilmanifold $X=X(\epsilon)$ of order 2 with respect to the filtration $G_{\bullet}$ such that for every $N\geq N_{0}$ and every $f\colon R_{\tilde{N}}\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ with
$\vert f\vert\leq 1$ and $\Vert f\Vert_{U^{3}(R_{\tilde{N}})}\geq\epsilon$, there exist a function $\Phi\colon X\rightarrow\mathbb{C}$ with $\Vert\Phi\Vert_{Lip(X)}\leq 1$ and a polynomial sequence $g(m,n)\colon [\tilde{N}]\times[\tilde{N}]\rightarrow G$ of degree 2 on $G$ with respect to $G_{\bullet}$ such that $\vert\mathbb{E}_{m+ni\in R_{\tilde{N}}}f(m+ni)\Phi(g(m,n)\cdot e_{X})\vert\geq\delta$.

nodes.name: Theorem 6.16
Proposition 7.25
Lemma 7.20
nodes.statement:
(Approximation property).
Let $\bold{\lambda}\in\mathbb{R}^{2}, \bold{\lambda}\neq(0,0)$. Set $\tilde{\alpha}=\theta^{-1}_{\bold{\lambda}}\alpha$.
Let $H$ be a subgroup of $H_{0}$. For every $C,D,\kappa>0, d\in\mathbb{N}$, there exist $C'=C'(X,C,\kappa,d), \kappa'=\kappa'(X,C,\kappa,d), D'=D'(X,C,D,\kappa,d)>0, N_{0}=N_{0}(X,C,\kappa,d)\in\mathbb{N}$ with the following property: Let $N\geq N_{0}$. Suppose that $g_{1}(n)=\prod_{i=0}^{d}\alpha_{i}^{\binom{n}{i}}, \alpha_{0},\dots,\alpha_{d-1}\in H, \alpha_{d}\in H_{2}$ is a $d$-polynomial which is not $S$-totally $\kappa$-equidistributed on $H$. Suppose also that
  $\bold{k}=p\underline{\bold{k}}\in\mathbb{Z}^{2s+2}$ is a vector of the same type as $H$ such that
   $H$ and $H^{\underline{\bold{k}}}$ are $\bold{\lambda}$-shaped,
   and that
   $0<\Vert\bold{k}\Vert\leq C, \Vert\bold{k}\cdot\tilde{\alpha_{i}}\Vert_{\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}\leq\frac{C}{N^{i}}$ for all $1\leq i\leq d-1$.

  Suppose that both $H$ and $H^{\underline{\bold{k}}}$ are $\bold{\lambda}$-shaped.
  Then there exists a polynomial sequence of the form $g_{2}(n)=\prod_{i=0}^{d}\beta_{i}^{\binom{n}{i}}$, $\beta_{0},\dots,\beta_{d}\in H^{\underline{\bold{k}}}$ such that

  1) If the pair $(H,H^{\underline{\bold{k}}})$ is good, then $g_{2}$ is not $S$-totally $\kappa'$-equidistributed on $H^{\underline{\bold{k}}}$;

2) If there exists $\bold{p}\in\mathbb{Z}^{2s+2}$ of the same type as $H$ (and thus of $H^{\underline{\bold{k}}}$) such that $0<\Vert\bold{p}\Vert\leq D$ and $\Vert\bold{p}\cdot\tilde{\beta_{1}}\Vert_{\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}\leq\frac{D}{N}$,
then there exists some $w\in\mathbb{Z}, 0<w\leq C^{2}$ such that $\Vert w\bold{p}\cdot\tilde{\alpha_{1}}\Vert_{\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}\leq\frac{D'}{N}$.

3) If $H_{2}=H_{2}^{\underline{\bold{k}}}$, then $\beta_{d}\in H_{2}^{\underline{\bold{k}}}$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.6
Theorem 7.3
nodes.statement:
(A variation of the quantitative Leibman Theorem).
  Let $X=G/\Gamma$ be a nilmanifold of order 2 and $t\in\mathbb{N}$. Then for any $\epsilon>0$ small enough, there exists $D=D(X,\epsilon,t)>0$ such that for any $N\in\mathbb{N}$ and any polynomial sequence $g\colon [\tilde{N}]^{t}\rightarrow G$, if $(g(\vec{n})\cdot e_{X})_{\vec{n}\in[\tilde{N}]^{t}}$ is not totally $\epsilon$-equidistributed, then there exists a horizontal character $\eta=\eta(X,\epsilon,t)$ such that $0<\Vert\eta\Vert\leq D$ and $\Vert \eta\circ g\Vert_{C^{\infty}[\tilde{N}]^{t}}\leq D$.

nodes.name: Theorem 7.5
nodes.statement:
(Inverse Leibman Theorem).
  Let $X=G/\Gamma$ be a nilmanifold of order 2 and $d\in\mathbb{N}$. There exists $C=C(X,d)>0$ such that for every $D>0$, every 2-tuple $\vec{N}=(N_{1},N_{2})\in\mathbb{N}^{2}$ with both $N_{1}$ and $N_{2}$ sufficiently large depending only on $X$ and $D$, and every polynomial map $g\colon [\vec{N}]\rightarrow G$ of degree at most $d$, if there exists a non-trivial horizontal character $\eta$ of $X$ with $\Vert\eta\Vert\leq D$ and $\Vert \eta\circ g\Vert_{C^{\infty}[\vec{N}]}\leq D$, then the sequence $(g(\vec{n})\cdot e_{X})_{\vec{n}\in[\vec{N}]}$ is not totally $CD^{-3}$-equidistributed in $X$.
